prompt.context: Our client, DigiBooks, is a manufacturer and seller of electronic book readers. DigiBooks also distributes e-books for the e-reader through their website. The reader is only compatible with books sold through the DigiBooks site. DigiBooks is planning the launch of its e-book readers in a country where no e-book readers are currently sold. Only 1% of the population has ever used an e-book reader, though 50% is aware of the concept. The Chief Marketing Officer of DigiBooks has come to you for help.
prompt.question: How should DigiBooks launch and market the e-reader product in this new country?

clarifying_info.q: What type of product is the e-reader?
clarifying_info.a: It uses an e-ink electronic paper display featuring 16 shades of grey, with a 12-hour battery life and easy readability.

clarifying_info.q: Has DigiBooks sold products outside the US before?
clarifying_info.a: No, DigiBooks has never sold a product outside of the US.

clarifying_info.q: Are there competitors in this new country?
clarifying_info.a: No competitors in the e-book or tablet space plan to enter this country.

exhibits.title: Market Segments
exhibits.shows: A table listing three reader segments (Super Readers, Occasional Readers, Rare Readers) with their segment size (in millions of people) and the e-reader price point for each segment.

exhibits.title: Channel Decisions
exhibits.shows: A table comparing the Retail and Internet sales channels across four metrics: percent of total potential market reached, e-book gross margin %, e-reader gross margin %, market penetration rate, and initial investment required.

framework: Segmentation, targeting and positioning: identify which population segments are the most valuable customers
Product: assess whether existing product meets needs or a new product must be developed for this country
Price: determine appropriate pricing for both the e-reader device and e-books; consider razor-and-blade pricing (low device price, higher book margin)
Promotion: decide on marketing and advertising mechanisms suited to this country
Place / Distribution: choose between retail stores, internet, or other channels
E-book selection: ensure sufficient local-language or relevant e-book catalog is available

questions.prompt: Using Exhibit 1 and a 3-year projection, which segment should the e-book reader target? (Ignore probability of purchase and time value of money; assume all reader sales happen immediately.)
questions.guidance: Candidate should calculate 3-year revenue potential for each segment using the formula: [(books/year x $10/book x 3 years) + (e-reader price x 1 unit)] x segment size. The missing data to surface: average e-book price is $10 across all segments; e-books and e-reader have the same margin. Compare totals and select the highest-revenue segment.

math.setup: Revenue = [(annual books x $10 x 3 years) + (e-reader price)] x segment size. E-book price = $10 (to be requested by candidate).
math.answer: Occasional Readers (OR) with a revenue potential of $8.5B

questions.prompt: DigiBooks is considering selling e-book readers through retail stores or through the internet. How would you evaluate this decision?
questions.guidance: Candidate should weigh pros and cons of each channel. Retail pros: encourages product trial, enables joint marketing with retailers, retailer handles customer service and returns. Retail cons: lower margin due to value chain intermediaries, time and cost to set up retail partnerships, training costs. Internet pros: cheaper to establish, higher margins. Internet cons: harder to encourage product trial, may limit reach to digitally connected consumers.

questions.prompt: DigiBooks has decided to price the e-reader at $100 and target the Occasional Reader segment (20M people). Using Exhibit 2, estimate the 1-year gross profit for each sales channel (after upfront investment). Which channel should DigiBooks choose?
questions.guidance: Candidate should calculate 1-year gross profit for Retail and Internet channels using: [(books/year x e-book price x e-book GM%) + (e-reader price x e-reader GM%)] x (segment size x penetration rate), then subtract initial investment. Use 10 books/year, $10/book from OR segment, $100 e-reader price, and market size of 20M from Exhibit 1.

math.setup: Annual profit = [(10 books x $10/book x e-book GM%) + ($100/e-reader x e-reader GM%)] x (20M people x penetration). Then subtract initial investment.
steps: (Note: casebook uses 10M people = half of 20M segment citing 50% of market reached by retail channel)
Casebook calculation: Retail = [($50 + $30)] x (20M x 50% channel reach x 40% penetration) - $20M = $80 x 4M - $20M = $320M - $20M = $300M
math.answer: Retail channel yields $300M profit vs. Internet $100M; choose Retail.

recommendation: DigiBooks should launch the e-reader targeting the Occasional Reader segment through the Retail sales channel
Expected 1-year gross profit of approximately $300M on an initial investment of $20M
risks: What retail channels already exist in the country? May need to create new channels
Do we have operational capacity to produce the required number of e-readers?
Should a local manufacturing facility be set up or should products be sourced from existing US facilities?
Are there prospects of competitors entering the market in future years?
Is there a sufficient e-book catalog available in the local language?
next_steps: Assess existing retail infrastructure and negotiate distribution partnerships
Evaluate supply chain and manufacturing capacity for the target volume
Define advertising and promotional strategy appropriate to this country
Monitor competitor landscape for potential new entrants
